event: Nala goes straight after the master, down the narrow back stair behind the tool racks.
The workshop is filling: apprentices in grey aprons settling at the long benches.
One grinding wheel on the east wall is already turning; the rest stand still.
The master takes her to a big, quiet man of about fifty, who walks with a lame leg.
"New bench hand," the master tells him. "Start her at the sorting table."
Then he goes back to his own bench under the north window and bends over his work.
The big man names himself, "Coyle," and takes a grey canvas apron and cotton gloves off a peg.
She hangs Maddox's coat on the peg and ties the apron over her loose grey shirt, twice round.
The sorting table stands by the door: trays of lens blanks, brass parts, a tin of spirit, rags.
Coyle shows her once: calliper to each blank, read the thickness, then try it on a gauge card.
Each blank goes into the tray the card names for its thickness.
The card lists thicknesses in lines and tenths, in plain numerals she reads at a glance.
Brass parts go in the spirit tin, get wiped with rag, and go back for repair.
Some parts come back warm and hum faintly if held too long.
Coyle tells her to leave a glyph on any repaired part alone until he has checked it.
At eight the rest of the wheels start up, a rising whine, then files and hammers under it.
At first the calliper is clumsy in her small fingers, and the jaws land a hair off each time.
By the second tray it sits right in her hand, and the blanks go where the card says.
Coyle limps by, tips out a tray, checks a dozen blanks with his own calliper, grunts, and moves on.
The morning goes by in blanks and brass. Her mouth is dry; the tea waits for noon, by the stove.
A girl of about seventeen slides onto the stool beside her with a tray of brass to clean.
She has ink on her fingertips, and she talks as she works: the call-up, her brother, exams.
She talks of the Chosen One on the news, and how nobody can say who it is.
Then she says her name is Tessa, and asks Nala where she's from. "Not round here, are you?"
Tessa waits, rag in hand, bright and curious, for the answer.
